1.1: Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy, who is their brother, to the well beloved Philemon, who shares our labours,
1.2: and to all the church that is in his household, to our dear sister Appia, Archippus, who fights the same battle with ourselves, and the rest;
1.3: Grace and peace be yours from God, our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.4: I give thanks to my God at all times, remembering thee in my prayers;
1.5: such accounts I hear of the love and faith thou shewest towards the Lord Jesus and towards all the saints.
1.6: May thy generosity in the faith be made known, when all your good actions are recognized in Christ Jesus.
1.7: It has been a happiness and a comfort to me to hear of thy charity, brother, and of the refreshment thou hast brought to the hearts of the saints.
1.8: And now, though I might well make bold in Christ to prescribe a duty to thee,
1.9: I prefer to appeal to this charity of thine. Who is it that writes to thee? Paul, an old man now, and in these days the prisoner, too, of Jesus Christ;
1.10: and I am appealing to thee on behalf of Onesimus, the child of my imprisonment.
1.11: He did thee an ill service once; now, both to thee and to myself, he can be serviceable,
1.12: and I am sending him back to thee; make him welcome, for my heart goes with him.
1.13: I would sooner have kept him here with me, to attend, as thy deputy, on a prisoner of the gospel,
1.14: but I would do nothing without thy leave; thy generosity should be exercised freely, not from lack of choice.
1.15: Perhaps, after all, the very purpose of thy losing him for a time was that thou mightest have him always by thee.
1.16: Do not think of him any longer as a slave; he is something more than a slave, a well loved brother, to me in a special way; much more, then, to thee, now that both nature and Christ make him thy own.
1.17: As thou dost value thy fellowship with me, make him welcome as thou wouldst myself;
1.18: if he has wronged thee, or is in thy debt, make me answerable for it.
1.19: Here is a message in Paul’s own hand; I will make it good. Not to remind thee that thou owest me a debt already, thy own self.
1.20: And now, brother, let me claim thy services; give comfort in the Lord to my anxious heart.
1.21: I write to thee counting on thy obedience, well assured that thou wilt do even more than I ask.
1.22: Be prepared, meanwhile, to entertain me; I hope, through your prayers, to be restored to you.
1.23: Greetings to you from Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus;
1.24: from Mark, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke, who share my labours.
1.25: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
